title: Roman inscription at Gobustan
description: A soldier of the Twelfth Legion carves the easternmost known Roman inscription among rock carvings that go back thousands of years.

title: Shirvanshahs become independent
description: The Arab governors of Shirvan make themselves independent of the caliphate and found a dynasty that lasts almost seven centuries.

title: Rus' raid on Barda
description: Raiders from Rus' sail up the Kura, seize the chief city of the region and hold it for months, and it never regains its place.

title: Ganja earthquake
description: An earthquake destroys Ganja and kills a very large number of its people, and a landslide on Mount Kapaz dams the valley that holds Lake Göygöl.

title: Birth of Nizami
description: Nizami Ganjavi, author of the five long Persian poems known as the Khamsa, is born in Ganja, where he spends his life.

title: Momine Khatun Mausoleum
description: The architect Ajami builds a brick tomb tower for the wife of the Eldiguzid ruler, the best known monument of the Nakhchivan school.

title: Palace of the Shirvanshahs
description: Shirvanshah Khalilullah I builds a palace in Baku, which had replaced Shamakhi as the capital.

title: Safavids annex Shirvan
description: Shah Tahmasp I ends the rule of the Shirvanshahs and makes their land a Safavid province.

title: Shamakhi earthquake
description: An earthquake destroys the city and kills about 80,000 people.

title: Russians take Baku
description: Baku surrenders to the forces of Peter the Great, which hold the Caspian coast for twelve years before returning it to Persia.

title: Shusha founded
description: Panah Ali Khan builds a fortress as the capital of the Karabakh Khanate, one of the khanates that arise after the death of Nader Shah.

title: Russians storm Ganja
description: The army of Pavel Tsitsianov takes the city and kills Javad Khan, which begins a nine-year war between Russia and Persia.

title: Treaty of Gulistan
description: Persia cedes to Russia most of what is now Azerbaijan north of the Aras, together with Dagestan and eastern Georgia.

title: Oil well drilled at Bibi-Heybat
description: A well is drilled for oil by mechanical means near Baku, among the first in the world and the start of the city's oil industry.

title: Nobel brothers found Branobel
description: The Nobel family's company introduces tankers and pipelines to Baku, which by 1901 produces half of the world's oil.

title: Armenian–Tatar massacres
description: Fighting between Armenians and Azerbaijanis breaks out in Baku and spreads across the Caucasus over the next two years, killing thousands on both sides.

title: March Days
description: Fighting for control of Baku between Bolshevik and Armenian forces and the Musavat party ends with the killing of thousands of Muslims.

title: Azerbaijan Democratic Republic declared
description: The Azerbaijani National Council declares independence, founding a parliamentary republic that gives women the vote.

title: Battle of Baku
description: An Ottoman and Azerbaijani army takes Baku from British, Armenian and Russian defenders, and thousands of Armenians are killed in the days that follow.

title: Red Army takes Baku
description: The Soviet Eleventh Army enters Baku and Azerbaijan becomes a Soviet republic.

title: Nagorno-Karabakh Autonomous Oblast created
description: Soviet authorities make the largely Armenian highlands of Karabakh an autonomous region within Soviet Azerbaijan.

title: Oil struck at Neft Daşları
description: A well in the open sea begins to flow, and a town on stilts grows up around one of the first offshore oil fields in the world.

title: Sumgait pogrom
description: Three days of attacks on the Armenians of Sumgait kill dozens of people and the Armenian population leaves the town.

title: Black January
description: Soviet troops enter Baku under a state of emergency, after a week of attacks on the city's Armenians, and kill more than a hundred civilians.

title: Independence restored
description: The Supreme Council adopts the constitutional act that restores the independence lost in 1920.

title: Khojaly massacre
description: Armenian forces capture the town during the Nagorno-Karabakh war and several hundred Azerbaijani civilians are killed.

title: Ganja revolt
description: A military mutiny led by Surat Huseynov brings down President Abulfaz Elchibey and returns Heydar Aliyev to power.

title: Ceasefire in the Nagorno-Karabakh war
description: A truce agreed at Bishkek takes effect, leaving Armenian forces in control of Nagorno-Karabakh and seven surrounding districts, with about 30,000 dead and a million displaced on both sides.

title: Contract of the Century
description: Azerbaijan signs an agreement with a group of foreign oil companies to develop the Azeri, Chirag and Gunashli fields in the Caspian.

title: Baku–Tbilisi–Ceyhan pipeline opened
description: A pipeline of 1,768 kilometres begins to carry Caspian oil to the Mediterranean without crossing Russia or Iran.

title: Four-day clashes
description: The heaviest fighting since the 1994 ceasefire breaks out along the line of contact around Nagorno-Karabakh and kills at least two hundred soldiers.
